newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-Pound to inflict pain on GrandMet.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Pound to inflict pain on GrandMet.

text.p: Britain's Smirnov vodka to Burger King group Grand Metropolitan Plc should report increased earnings at the half year stage on Thursday, although the effect of a strong pound will take its toll, analysts said on Friday.
"The results will show a strong underlying performance but all divisions will be hit by the currency impact through the period," said Warburg analyst John Spicer.
Analysts forecasts for pretax profits range from 461 to 477 million, up from 455 million last time. A dividend of 6.25p is expected, up from 5.85p.
Pillsbury, the group's U.S. food subsidiary is widely acknowledged as the real profit driver, forecast to turn in profits of some 255 million in the first half up from 237 million.
Burger King's earnings are expected to be broadly flat at 70 million, while the group's spirits arm is likely to show a near 10 million stg drop in profits to 202 million.
Of the spirits groups however analysts still favour GrandMet where overall spirits volumes are ahead of last year and conditions have improved in the United States.
Growth in spirits profits have been driven by higher levels of advertising expenditure compared to its peers and stronger price rises in most of IDV's major markets.
But there remains wide disagreement among analysts over the effect of currency translation on group profits.
Just six percent of GrandMet's profits are earned in Britain while 70 percent comes from the United States.

Although the company has a "cylinder" hedge for movements between $1.50 and $1.60 the company is unhedged to the pound but above that it is 80 percent hedged but this applies only to its dollar income.

Since the pound was consistently above $1.60 during the period the company had to stomach 20 percent of the exposure above this level. Analysts estimate the sterling/dollar impact should cost it about 13 million stg at the half year stage or 30 million stg at the full year.
